cohort: 400 children aged 0 to 6 years attending well baby clinics and daily pediatric outpatient departments for routine check-up and immunization in rural South India
finding: Language delay was seen in 9.5% of children, and was significantly associated with being a second-born child, not being a single child in the family, not living with both parents, preterm birth, caesarean birth, significant birth history, and not being exclusively breastfed.
mod_finding: Babies born by caesarean section had a significantly higher odds of language delay (OR 3.9).
gest_age: Preterm birth mentioned as a risk factor
